title: Free printable ADHD cleaning planner (weekly PDF, no email)
description: Free printable ADHD cleaning planner: a week of 10-minute resets, one named first step and a bad-day line per day. One-page PDF, direct download, no email.

faq.q: Is the ADHD cleaning planner really free?
faq.a: Yes. The PDF link on this page is a direct download. No email, no checkout, no trial. It is one A4 page, prints on any home printer, and you can print a fresh one every Monday.

faq.q: What is the difference between the planner and the checklist?
faq.a: The checklist is room by room: pick a room, run its reset. The planner is day by day: each weekday has one theme, one named first step and a bad-day line, so you never decide what to clean, only whether today is a low, mid or high energy day. Most people keep the checklist on the fridge and the planner on the wall by it.

faq.q: How long does each day take?
faq.a: Ten minutes on a mid day, twenty on a high day, and on a low day only the shaded bad-day line, which takes under a minute. The timer is the stop signal. Sunday has no cleaning at all: five minutes of setup for Monday and that is the whole job.

faq.q: What if I miss a day, or a whole week?
faq.a: Nothing carries over. No day depends on the one before it and the sheet restarts every Monday, so a missed Tuesday does not make Wednesday bigger. Three ticked boxes in a week is a good week; that number is on the sheet on purpose.

jsonld_extra.name: How to use the ADHD cleaning planner

step.name: Print it on Monday
step.text: Download the one-page PDF and print it. Put it on the wall where you will walk past it, not in a drawer. Circle one big thing for the week at the top, only one.

step.name: Tick today's energy
step.text: Low, mid or high. Low means you do only the shaded bad-day line. Mid is a 10-minute timer. High is 20 minutes and then you stop anyway.

step.name: Do the first step, only that
step.text: Each day names one physical first step. Do it without reading the rest of the row. Starting is the hard part; the step is chosen so it is impossible to get wrong.

step.name: Stop when the timer rings
step.text: Even mid-task. Tick the box. Take the reward you wrote at the top.

step.name: Sunday: no cleaning
step.text: Five minutes in the evening: tomorrow's clothes out, one clear surface, bag by the door. Then print next week's sheet.
